title: Paired Median-of-Means Rewards for Robust Configuration Selection in Vector Search Benchmarking

raw.stage1:
### Purpose:
The purpose of the contribution is to "reliably rank ANNS configurations despite environmental noise in wall-clock QPS measurements." None of the prior papers explicitly address this specific objective. While some papers discuss ranking (e.g., [13], [14], [27]) or robustness to noise (e.g., [7], [12], [19]), they do so in different contexts (e.g., ranking measures, information retrieval, or low-rank matrix recovery) and do not focus on the problem of ranking ANNS configurations under noisy conditions. Therefore, no prior paper covers this purpose.

### Mechanism:
The mechanism, "Paired Median-of-Means (Paired-MoM): paired randomized-order back-to-back execution of candidate and reference configs to cancel additive drift via log speedup ratios, plus median-of-means aggregation to suppress heavy-tailed outliers," involves two key components: (1) paired randomized-order execution to cancel drift and (2) median-of-means (MoM) aggregation for robustness to outliers. Several prior papers discuss MoM as a statistical method for handling noise and outliers (e.g., [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [7], [9], [26]), but none combine it with paired randomized-order execution or apply it to the specific problem of ranking ANNS configurations. The closest match is [8], which discusses paired comparison designs, but it focuses on experimental design rather than the specific mechanism of paired randomized-order execution combined with MoM aggregation. Thus, the mechanism is not covered.

### Evaluation:
The evaluation reports improvements in Kendall tau correlation for ranking ANNS configurations under noisy conditions. Kendall tau is a well-established metric for rank correlation, and its use in evaluation is covered by prior papers such as [14], [16], [20], and [27]. While the specific benchmarks (GIST-960 and SIFT-128) and the application to ANNS configurations are new, the evaluation design — using Kendall tau to measure ranking quality — is not novel. Therefore, the evaluation is covered.

### Domain:
The domain is "approximate nearest neighbor search benchmarking." This is a well-established area of research, and prior work such as [17] and [32] addresses benchmarking and robustness in related contexts. While the specific focus on ranking ANNS configurations under noisy conditions may be new, the general application area of ANNS benchmarking is not. Therefore, the domain is covered.
